intro: You are inside Mardin Museum, in Mardin province, opened in 1995. It lives in the 19th-century mansion of the Syriac patriarchate, and through the finds of Girnavaz and Dara it lays out the region's layers, from Assyria to the Artuqids.
history: The museum opened in 1995 in a mansion built at the end of the nineteenth century for the Syriac Catholic patriarchate. Its collection lets you read the region in layers: the Assyrian levels of the Girnavaz mound near Nusaybin, the Byzantine buildings of Dara, and the Artuqid work of the city all around you.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the patriarchal mansion itself, the finds from Girnavaz and the finds from Dara — and save time for the ethnography hall.
facts: Did you know? The building is part of the collection. The museum is housed in the mansion of the Syriac Catholic patriarchate, and nothing inside shows the carving of Mardin limestone at this scale: the finest example of Mardin stone carving here is the building itself. The collection also holds the finds from the Assyrian levels of the Girnavaz mound near Nusaybin.
outro: This brings our journey through Mardin Museum to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. Let these treasures stay bright for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
